primary_sources.title: q-Apery Irrationality Proofs by q-WZ Pairs
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Sections 1.3-1.5 define the q-WZ summand b(n,k), the summed sequence b(n), and L=y_2(n)N^2+y_1(n)N+y_0(n); summing the telescoping identity proves Lb=0. Section 1.6 writes the resulting scalar recurrence explicitly.
primary_sources.supports: The operator is derived as an annihilator of the specific q-WZ sum that becomes the p^(n+1) little-q-Legendre specialization.
primary_sources.does_not_support: No claim that the same L annihilates every moving evaluation of the little-q-Legendre kernel.

primary_sources.title: Little q-Legendre polynomials and irrationality of certain Lambert series
primary_sources.author: Walter Van Assche
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Equation (10) gives the finite little-q-Legendre sum. Equations (24)-(26) specialize at p^n; immediately after equation (25), Van Assche states that his P_n(p^n|q) is 'nearly' the Amdeberhan--Zeilberger b_n and identifies their value as P_n(p^(n+1)|q).
primary_sources.supports: Primary-source distinction between the two moving specializations of the common polynomial kernel.
primary_sources.does_not_support: No assertion that the Amdeberhan--Zeilberger scalar recurrence transfers to the p^n specialization.

primary_sources.title: Three Recitations on Holonomic Systems and Hypergeometric Series
primary_sources.author: Doron Zeilberger
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Tutorial development of recurrence operators, holonomic systems, and telescoping certificates for definite hypergeometric sums.
primary_sources.supports: Standard language in which an operator annihilates a declared sequence or sum and must be transported through an appropriate closure or telescoping argument.
primary_sources.does_not_support: No theorem that one operator is invariant under changing a moving specialization, and no little-q-Legendre comparison at issue here.

mechanism_comparison.standard_core: In holonomic/WZ practice, the recurrence is attached to the univariate sequence produced after a definite sum or specialization. A common underlying term or polynomial family does not by itself identify the annihilator ideals of two different resulting sequences.
mechanism_comparison.local_delta: The local checker substitutes the first three values of A_n=P_n(p^n|p^(-1)) into the operator derived for B_n=P_n(p^(n+1)|p^(-1)) and factors the index-zero residual as a strictly negative product for every p>1.
mechanism_comparison.terminology_boundary: 'Diagonal pullback' is understandable but risks collision with formal diagonal and D-finite closure terminology. 'Moving specialization' is more literal here; 'operator nontransfer' states exactly what the counterexample proves.
mechanism_comparison.remaining_route: The certificate excludes only the named Amdeberhan--Zeilberger operator. It neither denies holonomicity nor excludes a different scalar recurrence for A_n.
